rows.name: flagpole shaft
rows.notes: Left half of the 2px-wide flagpole shaft. CHR $1A2 in the BG pattern table $1000; read_tile shows one opaque column (index 1) at the tile's RIGHT edge, so when placed one nametable column left of $A3 the two columns join into the 2px pole. Nametable 0 columns 12 (this tile) and 13 ($A3) from row 6 (screen y48) down to row 19. Rendered lime green: index 1 = BG palette 0 slot 1 ($29). Proof: get_region object mode at the pole pixel (146,130) returned layer background, palette 0, slots [1], bbox (145,98)-(146,161) width 2, 119 px, CHR 0x1A2 + 0x1A3. Nametable read 0 (12,4) 4x20: rows 6-19 cols 12-13 = A2 A3 (rows 4 = 24, row 5 = 2F 3D the ball).
rows.why: the flagpole with the flag halfway down and Mario sliding, the castle beyond in this screenshot; CHR $1A2/$1A3 render as the one-pixel shaft halves, $12F/$13D as the ball halves, sprite $7E/$7F as the pennant

rows.name: flagpole ball
rows.notes: Left half of the ball/knob on top of the flagpole. CHR $12F in the BG pattern table $1000; read_tile shows a rounded shape hugging the tile's RIGHT edge (index 3 outline, index 1 highlight, index 2 fill). Placed at nametable 0 column 12, row 5 (screen y40-47), one column left of $3D, so together the two tiles form an ~8px ball centred on the pole. Colours: index 3 = BG palette 0 slot 3 $0F black outline, index 1 = slot 1 $29 lime, index 2 = slot 2 $1A green. Proof: get_region object mode at (146,46) returned layer background, palette 0, slots [1,2,3], bbox (142,40)-(149,77), CHR 0x12F,0x13D,0x1A2,0x1A3; nametable 0 (12,4) row 5 = 2F 3D.

rows.name: flagpole flag
rows.notes:
The flag on the flagpole is a SPRITE, not background: a 16x16 metasprite drawn from three OAM entries in sprite palette 5, positioned so it hangs on the pole's left side. Origin = top-left (130,91) in the frame captured at the flagpole (World 1-1, camera x=3030, Mario sliding down). OAM entries as (index, tile id, x offset, y offset from origin, flips):
- #10, $7E (126), (+0,+0), no flips - top-left quadrant (the diagonal pennant edge; read_tile $7E = a right-triangle of index 2).
- #11, $7F (127), (+8,+0), no flips - top-right quadrant (the flag's body/emblem; read_tile $7F = index-2 border around an index-1 field).
- #12, $7E (126), (+8,+8), no flips - bottom-right quadrant (the mirrored pennant edge).
There is no bottom-left entry, which gives the flag its pointed lower-left silhouette. The flag is drawn from SPRITE pattern table $0000 in SPRITE palette 5, live = [$0F,$1A,$30,$27] (slot 1 $1A green, slot 2 $30 white); rendered pixels sampled: get_pixel_color(138,94) = $1A green, get_pixel_color(134,94) = white (tile $7F uses index 1 for the field and index 2 for the border). PROOF: get_region object mode at (138,94) returned layer "sprite", palette 5, slots [1,2], 136 connected pixels, bbox (130,91)-(145,106) = 16x16, tiles [126,127], oam [10,11,12]; list_sprites at (138,94) hit OAM #11 tile $7F palette 5. The flag slides down the pole during the end-of-level sequence (it starts at the pole's top and descends with Mario).
rows.why: the flagpole with the flag halfway down and Mario sliding, the castle beyond in this screenshot; CHR $1A2/$1A3 render as the one-pixel shaft halves, $12F/$13D as the ball halves, sprite $7E/$7F as the pennant
